_comment: Qwen3.5/3.6 multi-token-prediction head. It ships inside its target's HF checkpoint, so its configs are the target's verbatim HF config (which declares `mtp_num_hidden_layers`) and it registers under the identity `qwen3_5_mtp` — the `model_type` MLX gives the head's separate drafter repo (named from the target's: `org/X-4bit` → `org/X-MTP-4bit`, `drafter_repo_infix`), whose tensors are stored bare (`fc.*`, `layers.0.*`, `norm.*`, `pre_fc_norm_*`; hence the empty decoder prefix). It has no embed_tokens / lm_head of its own: the loader lends it the target's. Its decoder layers are the MTP layers, so `num_hidden_layers` REPLACES the backbone's count with `mtp_num_hidden_layers`. Norms as the Qwen3.5 family (zero-centered on HF checkpoints; MLX-affine ones store the full gain, which the norm offset rule reads as-is); the routed experts renormalize top-k as the target's. It DRAFTS OVER A VOCABULARY PREFIX: its logits are the target lm_head's first 65536 rows (`vocab_size`; token ids in BPE merge order, the most frequent first), so a draft costs a quarter of the 248k-row lm_head read; it embeds every token (`embed_vocab_size`). Every emitted token is still the target's choice (a draft is only a proposal it verifies); what the prefix costs is the drafts it cannot make: on the MLX oracle (k=3, code/story/repeat prompts) 2.85 tokens per verify step against 2.94 at the full vocabulary. It drafts `spec_drafts` tokens a step while the step holds at most `spec_max_seqs` sequences: one, the point measured to pay on both GPUs measured (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, one request, with drafts vs without: base M5 output tok/s 1.36-1.38x sampled; M5 Max TPOT 1.14x sampled, 1.28x greedy, on an earlier build of this head). Past it a verify step's three rows a sequence read the experts of three times the rows, and where that stops paying depends on the GPU (base M5: up to 4 sequences) and on the target (a dense one's rows cost far less).
